number.why: The source explicitly prints RR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.65) for recurrent pericarditis and identifies the primary analysis population as intention-to-treat. However, the packet does not establish that this estimate represents the longest reported recurrence follow-up. The registry specifies a planned 18-month outcome without linking it to the reported estimate. Thus the numerical transcription is correct, but full confirmation of the served outcome is unsupported.

quotes.span: The primary outcome was recurrent pericarditis in the intention-to-treat population.

The proportion of patients who had recurrent pericarditis was 26 (21·6%) of 120 in the colchicine group and 51 (42·5%) of 120 in the placebo group (relative risk 0·49; 95% CI 0·24-0·65; p=0·0009; number needed to treat 5).
PROTOCOL PRIMARY OUTCOME: Recurrence rate at 18 months |  | TIME FRAME: 18 m onths

entry.why: Adults with multiple recurrences explicitly meet the question's population. Random assignment, placebo control, masking, and colchicine added to conventional anti-inflammatory therapy are established.

quotes.span: Adult patients with multiple recurrences of pericarditis (≥two) were randomly assigned (1:1) to placebo or colchicine (0·5 mg twice daily for 6 months for patients weighing more than 70 kg or 0·5 mg once daily for patients weighing 70 kg or less) in addition to conventional anti-inflammatory treatment with aspirin, ibuprofen, or indometacin.
Patients and all investigators were masked to treatment allocation.

missed: The ruling acknowledges the follow-up gap but does not carry that uncertainty into SERVED_CONFIRMED. Also, the quoted arm counts imply a crude RR of (26/120)/(51/120) = 0.5098, rather than 0.49. The ruling records this alternative, but the packet does not explain the discrepancy. It does not justify replacing the explicitly printed estimate or relabelling it as a different estimand.
